definitions.gloss: with shoes on, shod feet, outdoor footwear
definitions.explanation: Wearing shoes indoors or in a place where shoes should be removed. In Japanese culture, entering a home or certain buildings with shoes on is a significant breach of etiquette.

examples.japanese: {土足|どそく}⟦{厳禁|げんきん}→厳禁：18021_genkin⟧。
examples.english: No shoes allowed. (Lit: Shod feet strictly prohibited.)

examples.japanese: {土足|どそく}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{家|いえ}→家：00612_ie⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{上|あ}がらないで→上がる：00615_agaru⟧⟦ください→下さい：02899_kudasai⟧。
examples.english: Please don't come into the house with your shoes on.

examples.japanese: ⟦{泥棒|どろぼう}→泥棒：01688_dorobou⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{土足|どそく}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧まま⟦{家|いえ}→家：00612_ie⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{中|なか}→中：00654_naka⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{歩|ある}き{回|まわ}った→歩き回る：04605_arukimawaru⟧⟦{形跡|けいせき}→形跡：17133_keiseki⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦あった→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: There were traces of a burglar having walked around inside the house with shoes on.

notes:
CULTURAL NOTE:
In Japan, removing shoes before entering homes, temples, some restaurants, and other buildings is a deeply rooted custom. Entering {土足|どそく}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧ (with shoes on) is considered extremely rude and unhygienic. Signs reading {土足|どそく}⟦{厳禁|げんきん}→厳禁：18021_genkin⟧ (shoes strictly prohibited) or {土足|どそく}⟦{禁止|きんし}→禁止：02643_kinshi⟧ (no shoes) are common at entrances.

The phrase {土足|どそく}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{踏|ふ}み{込|こ}む→踏み込む：06972_fumikomu⟧ literally means "to step in with shoes on" and is used figuratively to mean intruding into someone's private affairs.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {土足|どそく}⟦{厳禁|げんきん}→厳禁：18021_genkin⟧: shoes strictly prohibited
- {土足|どそく}⟦{禁止|きんし}→禁止：02643_kinshi⟧: no shoes allowed
- {土足|どそく}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{上|あ}がる→上がる：00615_agaru⟧: to enter with shoes on
- {土足|どそく}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{踏|ふ}み{込|こ}む→踏み込む：06972_fumikomu⟧: to barge in (figurative)
